meta.title: Sears Invented Shopping From Home. It Still Went Bankrupt.
meta.hook: Sears helped teach America to shop from home, then entered bankruptcy after shopping moved to screens.
meta.description: Sears' mail-order catalog, launched in 1893, once sold everything from tools to entire houses and made it the largest retailer in the US. The company that pioneered remote shopping never fully made the leap to e-commerce, and filed for Chapter 11 bankruptcy on October 15, 2018.

scenes.narration: Sears helped teach America to shop from home, then entered bankruptcy after shopping moved to screens.

visual.decision_reason: hook beat: the irony stated upfront

scenes.narration: Its famous catalogs connected distant households to an enormous range of merchandise delivered through a national distribution system.

scenes.narration: That model reduced the importance of a nearby store: customers could browse at home and order remotely.

visual.decision_reason: widely reported peak-era retail dominance, marked probable for the exact ranking era

scenes.narration: But retail shifted again toward e-commerce, faster fulfillment, and competitors built specifically around digital shopping.

scenes.narration: Sears still carried the cost and complexity of a huge physical-store network while its core business weakened.

scenes.narration: On October fifteenth, twenty eighteen, Sears Holdings filed for Chapter Eleven protection.
